title: Ins & Outs of 2026
html:
I started writing my last post on a train in Denmark. I’m starting this post sitting on a pad with no shoes on in a cozy little Copenhagen matcha shop. Shoutout Matcha MORI. Today’s drink of choice is a Matcha Yuzu Fizz. I’m honestly not quite sure what to make of it, but it’s definitely not boring! Would recommend.

It’s nearly 2026, so it’s time to do some reflecting. For me, 2025 was, to put it succinctly, fucked up—lots of pain; lots of learning. I’m grateful for this chapter, and I’m ready to close it.

Let’s do it.

In: Sleep. Nuff said.

Out: Caffeine abuse—in service of the first In. I think I averaged 400mg a day in 2025 (about 4.5 cups of coffee).

In: Employment. I'm done with college (for now, at least)—time to become a real adult.

Out: Staring into the abyss of the unknown, unemployed, and without feeling a sense of place. I have no choice but to do some abyss-staring in 2026 before I solidify my next steps and find a job, but I’ll do my best to do it with grace. ‘Tis but a season of life. It sucks, and that’s okay.

In: Regular phone calls with people that matter to me. I have repeating calendar events to call people with whom it’s imperative for me to maintain a healthy relationship. Relationships don’t maintain themselves. They need regular input. So I’m inputting!

Out: No more loved ones almost dying multiple times in rapid succession, please. You know who you are. Stop that *shakes finger sternly*. At least get old first if you’re going to pull that crap on us. Love you😘.

In: Trusting my gut about people, especially as it pertains to dating. I tend to draw conclusions about people quickly, but the scientist in me reminds me I should keep an open mind and collect more data. After all, how can I make conclusions about my data if I haven’t even seen what their trends over time look like? As much as I’d love to say that my open and curious approach has served me well, and that I’ve been shown again and again that my initial judgments about people are often proven wrong, it hasn’t, and I haven’t. It’s gotten me into some sticky situations, and, in some cases, caused far more harm than good. And for the harm done, I’m deeply sorry. A friend once told me that one of the hardest things to learn in life is how to grieve the pain we’ve caused others. I’m still working on that, but we’re getting there. For 2026, I should take action on my assessments more quickly. If it’s not a “Hell ya!”, it’s a “No”… even if they’re really, really pretty *sigh*.

Out: College. After finishing 18th grade and earning my MS, I think I’m done. I KNOW I’m fed up, but I also think I’m done. The last time I thought I was done, I continued and got my master’s. Maybe this time I’ll go do a PhD in Copenhagen or something. Who knows. Life is silly and unreasonable sometimes (basically all the time). This, however, seems unlikely. I’m deeply grateful for the incredible opportunities I had at university, but, respectfully, academia can suck my balls. Let’s see if I can find myself a big-boy job in the “real world” in 2026 :)

In: More friend time. My closest friends live in different states, and I seldom get to see them. Still, from a distance, they’ve seen me through all my 2025 woes with unwavering support. They watched me make some really dumb decisions and helped me avoid even dumber ones. I should spend more time with these guys.

Out: Balding. I’m 23. This is silly. It’s not my time yet. I’m going to solve this with pharmacology.

In: Girlfriend. Currently (December 2025) single and accepting girlfriend applications. I may have fallen a little in love with a Danish girl on my trip, but I’m not sure if that one will work out. A man can dream, though, can’t he? Maybe I’ll be going back to Denmark sooner than I thought.

Out: Noise. Shorts, reels, stories, etc. They rarely add value; they usually add noise. I don’t have Instagram, TikTok, or X, but I’m as guilty as anyone for falling into YouTube shorts wormholes that suck up hours of your time and leave you feeling disoriented and regretful. I recognized that I often feel the same or worse after consuming short-form content, but I seldom feel better. This is why I deleted my other social media accounts in the first place. My ability to focus gets compromised because I shoot a firehose of information at my brain—not a drop of which is useful. It’s just noise, and it makes my brain feel all fuzzy. On top of the fuzziness, way too many of my 2025 nights ended with me being washed up and ready for bed at a reasonable hour, then pissing away my chances of a good night's sleep by watching clickbaity YouTube shorts. ‘Tis unacceptable. I need to be better about this in 2026.

In: Swiss cheese stacks of hobbies. I wrote a post called “Instant Pots and Swiss Cheese” that almost nobody read 😂🤷‍♂️. It’s actually my worst-performing post to date. I’m unsure why, but I think there’s something of real value there, so give it a read. The crux of it is that my hobbies—although some could be considered lifestyle choices—are diverse. And this diversity enriches who I am as a person while simultaneously providing me with healthy coping mechanisms that keep me (mostly) sane. The current stack, as listed in my post, is: weight training, jiu-jitsu, playing music (guitar, piano, etc.), walking, writing.

From “Instant Pots and Swiss Cheese”:

“‘Life is pain, Highness. Anyone who says differently is selling something.’ — Wesley, The Princess Bride

In short, Wesley is right. Life is pain. And we can either let it consume us, or we can cope. Effective coping requires a diverse set of strategies that achieves complete coverage of our needs. With my cheese stack as inspiration, I encourage you to think about your own from first principles, find its holes, and determine how to cover them up.’

Out: Letting my fear of what others think keep me acting. Two things I’m certain of: most people don’t care what I do, and most of the opinions of the people who do care don’t matter. Taken together, there’s no good reason that I shouldn’t try to extract as much from life as I can: to try and fail, to make a fool of myself, to aspire to act with such kindness and generosity that it confuses people, to avoid playing zero-sum games, to build something new and useful, and to leave the world better than when I found it. We’re all going to be dead soon enough (unless we achieve longevity escape velocity 🙊). It’d be a tragedy to let fear keep us from finding out how incredible our lives could be. Here’s to taking action in 2026.

In: Joy, wonder, and adventure. The weather in my life from 2020 to 2025 has been rather cloudy and gray, with 2025 in particular being cloudy with a chance of getting my emotional nuts kicked in every other month. In college, I didn’t make time for much besides work and working out because I was committed to performing well without sacrificing my physical well-being. I took on multiple research roles (in series, not in parallel), published a paper, graduated with excellent GPAs, and stayed healthy. But all this was at the cost of joy, wonder, and adventure. This chapter is closing now. Soon enough, I’ll be working a real job, in a new place, surrounded by new people. I’m staring at blank pages, and I intend to write this next chapter much more colorfully. I’ll let you all know how it goes, but feel free to send me a message in the meantime if you’re getting antsy for updates :)

TLDR:

Ins:

  • Sleep

  • Employment

  • Regular phone calls with people that matter to me

  • Trusting my gut about people, especially as it pertains to dating

  • More friend time

  • Girlfriend

  • Swiss cheese stack of hobbies

  • Joy, wonder, and adventure

Outs:

  • Caffeine abuse—in service of the first In

  • Staring into the abyss of the unknown, unemployed, and without feeling a sense of place

  • No more loved ones almost dying multiple times in rapid succession, please

  • College

  • Balding

  • Noise

  • Letting my fear of what others think keep me acting

I wish everyone a beautiful 2026.

Much love,

Charlie ❤️
